Why Plano businesses miss calls

Plano is home to Toyota Motor North America, a large JPMorganChase campus and the Legacy West district. Over one in five working residents is in professional, scientific or management services, and household incomes are high. Clients here compare firms quickly, and a voicemail can feel like a closed door. A clear, professional AI greeting protects that first impression.

Which Plano businesses benefit most?

  • Law firms: New clients can reach intake after hours, and your team gets a short summary.
  • Accountants and CPAs: Tax season calls can be answered and booked without pulling staff from client work.
  • Dental offices: Busy professionals often call during lunch or after work, when the front desk is full.

Can you keep your Plano phone number?

Yes. Plano callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
